_meta.business: Bonefirm — bone & joint supplement for women 45+ through menopause
_meta.form_fidelity: What the founder would have typed at engagement start. Deliberately preserves the founder's own framing — including the flaws the analysis later corrected. Written BEFORE reading the conclusion.
_meta.labelled_verdict_note: Held separately from this file. Not shown to the scorer.

form.category: Health supplements — bone and joint support for women going through menopause. Daily capsule. Made in Singapore, GMP-certified. Non-hormonal.
form.positioning_sentence: The only supplement Asian women need for their bones through menopause — a non-hormonal structural system built on NEM eggshell membrane plus a blend of traditional Chinese botanicals.
form.differentiator: We are the only ones combining a clinically-studied Western ingredient (NEM eggshell membrane) with traditional Chinese medicine botanicals. It is an East-meets-West formula. The complete system is seven ingredients: NEM as the structural foundation, plus Salvia miltiorrhiza (Danshen), Ligusticum chuanxiong, Morus alba, Dendrobium officinale, Rosa rugosa, and Vitamin C. It is not a single component with extras bolted on — it is formulated as a system, designed as a whole rather than in parts. The botanicals support circulation and tissue nourishment, which is what NEM needs to work in the body. GMP-manufactured in Singapore. Developed with experts in Singapore and the United States, and it took real formulation work to get the combination to this point — this is not something I could have put together by buying ingredients off a shelf.
form.undercut_on: Price. Anyone can buy NEM capsules on their own from Watsons or online for much less. Competitors also keep launching cheaper versions of the same thing.
form.their_price_point: I don't know exactly. Probably S$0.50 to S$1 a day for the pharmacy brands.

customer_description: Women 45 and above going through menopause. Also their daughters — a lot of our buyers are women in their 20s and 30s buying for their mother.

_notes_for_harness.why_these_answers: Chosen to preserve the founder's own framing. The positioning sentence is her stated claim, superlative included ('the only supplement Asian women need'). She names 5 competitors, all of them the OBVIOUS ones — the pharmacy and retail brands — and does not name the global menopause symptom brands (Midi, Nutrafol, The Better Menopause) that the analysis treats as the real category competitors.
flaws_preserved: Analyst jargon in her own mouth: 'non-hormonal structural system' — the analysis later found nobody understands this phrase and replaced it with 'bones and joints, without hormones'
The superlative 'the only supplement Asian women need' — unprovable, later dropped
Competitor set is the retail shelf, not the menopause category — misses the real competitive frame
Undercut on price only — no mention of the menopause-specific position at all

Customer description is a DEMOGRAPHIC ('women 45+'), not a customer with a trigger, need and willingness to pay. The analysis's central correction. Note she adds the daughter observation herself, which is real and unprompted.

corrections_after_sean_review_2026_09_23.what_changed: The differentiator field was too thin. It named three botanicals as a list and omitted the FORMULATION claim the live site actually makes. Corrected to reflect bonefirm.com/pages/the-science: seven named ingredients, 'designed as a whole, not in parts', the botanicals supporting the conditions NEM needs, and 'developed with experts in Singapore and the United States'.
corrections_after_sean_review_2026_09_23.why_it_matters: This was a REAL input-fidelity defect, not a labelling dispute. The original file under-stated the differentiator relative to what the founder's own website claims. Jev scored defensibility 2 on the thin version — which was a correct reading of the thin version. Garbage in, correct garbage-out.
corrections_after_sean_review_2026_09_23.the_real_tension: The site under-claims the integration in its marketing copy while the founder over-claims the R&D privately. The form is the wrong instrument to distinguish a designed formulation from a cosmetic blend — it can only read the claim. This is a rubric limitation, to be recorded.
corrections_after_sean_review_2026_09_23.honest_note_on_provenance: The formulation detail is verifiable from the public site. The claim that the founder 'underwent significant R&D' is the client's assertion, and the analysis itself does not record it — so the reconstruction states what the site supports and stops there.

context_the_analysis_had_that_is_deliber: The NUH/NUS finding that Asian women rank joint pain #1 (32.9%) and hot flashes 5th (18.6%) — the analysis's central wedge, and the founder did not know it
That NEM is a commodity, not a moat
That the silent-risk-aware woman is the beachhead
